title: Other Senior Officials: Waivers, Late Divestitures & Outside Interests
summary: Filings document a small set of published conflict-of-interest waivers (Kennedy's interim waiver for family-office funds, Wright's CERAWeek waiver, plus Sacks, Lutnick and one task-force official), retained interests approved in ethics agreements (Patel's Elite Depot units, Isaacman's Shift4 stake), a missed certification deadline flagged for McMahon by the Campaign Legal Center, and a gap between Kennedy's amended ethics agreement and how his Gardasil fee interest was actually assigned, according to HHS's own letter as quoted by senators. Musk served without a public disclosure or published waiver. Bisignano's Fiserv sale met its deadline, and nothing late was found for Oz, Hegseth or Boulos. The oversight offices changed sharply: the OGE director was removed in Feb 2025 and the office has been run by acting heads with other jobs or left vacant; a court found the Jan 2025 IG removals unlawful but did not reinstate anyone; Biden's ethics pledge was revoked without replacement. No authority has found that any named official violated 18 U.S.C. 208 or an ethics agreement.

sub_claims.statement: Elon Musk served as a special government employee without a public financial disclosure or a published conflict-of-interest waiver while his companies held federal contracts and faced federal regulators; he left in late May 2025.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented status, no finding. Rule: as a special government employee (SGE, at most 130 days in 365) Musk was covered by 18 U.S.C. 208, which bars work on particular matters affecting his financial interests unless a 208(b) waiver or exemption applies. Filing: a White House official said in February 2025 that he would file a confidential (non-public) report, which SGEs may do (AP via Star-Advertiser, excerpt). Waiver: none appears on the White House list of 208(b)(1) waivers (read in full, Nov 2026: Kennedy, Leder, Lutnick, Sacks twice, Wright). Letters: Sen. Schiff asked OGE Director Huitema on 10 Feb 2025, the day Huitema was removed, whether any waiver existed (read in full); House Oversight Democrats asked White House Counsel Warrington on 1 May 2025 for the disclosure and any 208(b) determination (read in full). Exposure: a Senate PSI minority staff memo (27 Apr 2025, excerpt) counted 65 actions by 11 agencies against Musk's companies and estimated at least $2.37B of potential liability for 40 of them; this is a partisan staff estimate, not a finding. Departure: Musk announced on 28 May 2025 that his SGE time was ending (ABC, excerpt). The Campaign Legal Center asked OGE in June 2025 to check DOGE staff's disclosure compliance (read in full). Response: Press Secretary Leavitt said Musk would excuse himself from conflicting contracts (quoted in the Schiff letter). No OGE, inspector-general or court finding on his compliance was found. Builds on C68 (contracts, IPO).

sub_claims.statement: Kash Patel kept his Elite Depot (Shein parent) stock units as FBI director, and his ethics agreement records other outside interests.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (ethics agreement of 28 Jan 2025, read in full). Section 7: he ended his Elite Depot consulting on 1 Jan 2025 and keeps vested and unvested restricted stock units vesting quarterly to 1 Nov 2025. The Justice Department determined divestiture was 'not necessary at this time' because matters affecting the company were 'remote', so he recuses from such matters instead; this is not a waiver and not a late divestiture. The value was $1M-$5M on his nominee report (Schiff letter, excerpt). Other terms: resign from Trump Media's board (the 28 Jan 2025 share award is covered in C65); a one-year 'covered relationship' with Qatar after consulting for its embassy until Nov 2024, with a written authorization to participate 'will' be granted (whether it was is not public); divest 19 stocks (including Nvidia, Palantir, Rumble, MP Materials) within 90 days. Letter: Sen. Schiff and colleagues objected on 12 Feb 2025 to the retained Shein stake. No certification-of-compliance problem, waiver or finding was found. Response: Patel told senators he would not take part in matters affecting Elite Depot.

sub_claims.statement: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. received an ethics waiver, and his Gardasil referral-fee interest was handled differently from his ethics agreement.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented waiver and documented discrepancy; no finding. Waiver: White House Counsel Warrington issued a 'limited, interim' 208(b)(1) waiver on 18 Feb 2025 covering four Park Holdings Group funds (under $380,000 in total) until they could be divested in April 2025 (read in full). Fees: his 21 Jan 2025 agreement kept a 10% contingency-fee interest in cases referred to Wisner Baum; the 1 Feb 2025 amended agreement said he would 'irrevocably' assign it to a non-dependent adult son. According to Sen. Warren and colleagues' letter of 24 Sept 2026 (excerpt), an HHS letter of 25 Aug 2026 said he instead assigned the interest to Wisner Baum on 11 Feb 2025, two days before his confirmation, and his 12 May 2025 compliance certification did not mention this. The senators say OGE approval is required to change an agreement and ask whether any future-payment understanding exists; Merck settled most Gardasil suits for about $50M on 4 June 2026 (Bloomberg, as cited). Response: Kennedy posted on 1 Aug 2026 that he relinquished the interest to the firm before taking office; HHS said it confirmed his compliance in May 2025 (AP, excerpt). No OGE determination was found.

sub_claims.statement: Mehmet Oz divested late or incompletely.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: pledge documented; compliance not established. His ethics agreement (Feb 2025) committed him to sell dozens of health holdings (including UnitedHealth, AbbVie, Eli Lilly, McKesson) and his $5M-$25M of iHerb units within 90 days of confirmation and to leave iHerb and Eko Health roles, while keeping interests such as Oz Media and a ranch (NPR, Fierce Healthcare, excerpts). An ethics lawyer called the iHerb wording ambiguous. We found no compliance certification, Senate or OGE letter, waiver or finding about late divestiture; no response was needed.

sub_claims.statement: Pete Hegseth's broker approached BlackRock about a defence-fund investment before the Iran strikes.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: single-source (Financial Times, 30 Mar 2026, as recorded in C103). The reported approach was not executed. Letters: Warner and Schiff to the SEC and DoD inspector general (2 Apr 2026, read in full in C103) and Warren to the SEC (20 Apr 2026). Response: the Pentagon denied that Hegseth or any representative approached BlackRock. No waiver, investigation result or finding was found. Not repeated here beyond C103.

sub_claims.statement: Chris Wright received an ethics waiver while divesting Liberty Energy.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (waiver of 7 Mar 2025, pages 1-2 read). A limited 208(b)(1) waiver let him discuss energy policy at CERAWeek on 10-11 Mar 2025 while still holding Liberty Energy stock and three CAZ private-equity funds. It records an OGE certificate of divestiture (18 Feb 2025), 2,582,967 Liberty shares as of 18 Feb, a daily selling plan to finish by 21 Mar 2025, and CAZ funds to be exited by 1 Apr 2025 (he was confirmed 3 Feb 2025, so all within 90 days). His 278-T reports self-certify 11 of 301 transactions as reported late (Open Cabinet count). No late-divestiture finding.

sub_claims.statement: Doug Burgum's divestitures or disclosures were late, and Interior has unresolved ethics questions.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented reporting lag; no finding. He pledged to divest oil and gas lease interests and other holdings within 90 days and reportedly filed his compliance certification (Ground News summary, excerpt). His 278-T reports self-certify 106 of 153 transactions as reported late (Open Cabinet, from his filings); that is late reporting, not late divestiture. Separately, Interior released redacted ethics records in Feb 2026 for appointee Karen Budd-Falen over ties to the Thacker Pass lithium project; a conservation group asked for an inspector-general inquiry (High Country News, excerpt). No waiver or finding for Burgum was found.

sub_claims.statement: Linda McMahon missed her divestiture deadline.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented complaint; no finding. Her ethics agreement (5 Feb 2025) listed 81 holdings, 78 of them school and university bonds, to sell within 90 days of her 3 Mar 2025 confirmation, i.e. by 1 June 2025. The Campaign Legal Center told OGE (acting director Greer) on 9 July 2025 that no compliance certification or transaction report had been made public more than a month after the deadline (complaint, pages 1-3 read). Her later 278-T filings list transactions from 19 Dec 2024 to 24 June 2025, with 153 of 156 self-certified as late (Open Cabinet); whether the post-deadline sales were ethics-agreement assets is not shown. No OGE response or finding was found; no response from McMahon was found.

sub_claims.statement: Kelly Loeffler kept outside interests of note while running the SBA.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented holdings; no finding. Fortune (June 2025, excerpt) reported she held Newsmax parent stock not on her divestiture list while appearing on Newsmax; the SBA said she complied with her agreement and OGE had reviewed her holdings. NOTUS (11 Feb 2026, read in full) reported a $3M investment in Groq through Descante Capital LLC in Oct 2025, weeks before Groq's $20B Nvidia licensing deal; the SBA said her portfolio is 'independently managed without her direction or input'. A filing published by NOTUS (named as a 278-T of 21 Nov 2025) lists a sale of Intercontinental Exchange stock, her husband's company, of $5M-$25M on 19 Nov 2025 (as summarised in search results; the form was not read). No waiver, letter result or finding was found.

Grade: documented. His ethics agreement required selling Fiserv within 120 days of his 6 May 2025 confirmation (Payments Dive, excerpt). Senators Warren and Wyden say he held about $594M of Fiserv stock at confirmation and sold it between 16 May and 1 July 2025 for about $530M, before the stock roughly halved in late Oct 2025; they wrote to Fiserv in Nov 2025 asking what he knew. The sale was within the deadline. Response: his agency said he complied with all obligations of his ethics agreement (GovExec, excerpt). No finding.

sub_claims.statement: Jared Isaacman kept a large stake in Shift4 at NASA.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (ethics agreement of 17 Nov 2025, relevant sections read). He keeps Shift4 Payments equity, gives up majority voting control (to about 25%), ends a tax receivable agreement and recuses from matters affecting Shift4 unless waived; the agreement lists other assets to sell within 90 days. Sludge (June 2026, excerpt) reported 278-T purchases of Shift4 stock of $5M-$25M each on 11 and 12 May 2026, weeks before the SpaceX IPO (Shift4 has a SpaceX relationship). His 278-T reports self-certify 128 of 147 transactions as late (Open Cabinet). Buying a retained, recused holding is not barred by the agreement; no waiver, letter outcome or finding was found.

sub_claims.statement: Massad Boulos has an ethics waiver or late filing on record.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: nothing located. We found no public financial disclosure, ethics agreement, waiver, letter or finding for Boulos as senior adviser; the White House waiver list does not include him. C65 found no personal benefit from his DRC mediation. This is an absence of public records, not evidence either way.

sub_claims.statement: The White House has published only a handful of conflict-of-interest waivers, and no new ethics pledge replaced the one revoked on 20 Jan 2025.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented. On 20 Jan 2025 the President revoked EO 13989 (the Biden appointee ethics pledge) and issued no replacement pledge as of reporting we found (AP, Jan 2025; Campaign Legal Center, 23 Jan 2025, read in full); our searches found no later pledge order through Nov 2026, but this is an absence of results. Without a pledge there are no pledge waivers to post. The White House disclosures page (read in full, Nov 2026) lists six 208(b)(1) waivers: Kennedy (18 Feb 2025), Sacks (5 Mar and June 2025), Wright (7 Mar 2025), Lutnick (July 2025) and Jetson Leder Luis of the anti-fraud task force (16 Apr 2026, spouse's Amazon units). Agency-issued waivers go to OGE's collection, which we could not search.

sub_claims.statement: The OGE director was removed in February 2025 and the office has since been run by acting heads with other jobs or left without one.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented. OGE posted on 10 Feb 2025 that the President was removing Director David Huitema (confirmed Dec 2024 for a five-year term; read in full). Acting heads: VA Secretary Doug Collins (Feb 2025), Trade Representative Jamieson Greer (about Apr to Sept 2025, also acting Special Counsel), OMB deputy Eric Ueland (from about Aug/Sept 2025) (CREW, read in full; senators' letter). Senators wrote on 18 May 2026 that Ueland's service ended in early Dec 2025, that the 300-day acting limit had expired and OGE had no leader even in an acting capacity (read in full). On 23 June 2026 the President nominated Michael Chamberlain as director and named Acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling acting director (OGE release, read in full). We found no confirmation vote for Chamberlain as of Nov 2026. Huitema said the firing did not appear personal (CBS, via search).

sub_claims.statement: Inspectors general were dismissed in January 2025, a court found the removals unlawful, and they were not reinstated.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented. On 24 Jan 2025 more than a dozen IGs (about 17) were removed by a two-sentence email citing 'changing priorities', without the 30-day notice to Congress and case-specific reasons the IG Act requires. Eight sued (Storch v. Hegseth, D.D.C.). On 24 Sept 2025 Judge Ana Reyes found the President had almost certainly violated the IG Act but denied reinstatement for lack of irreparable harm, leaving back pay open, and stayed the rest pending Trump v. Slaughter (Clearinghouse summary, read in full; Washington Times, GovExec, excerpts). The Supreme Court decided Slaughter on 29 June 2026, 6-3, overruling Humphrey's Executor for FTC commissioners (law-firm summaries, excerpt); we did not find a later ruling in Storch. Later counts: Cato (Apr 2026) says at least 21 IGs were fired, forced out or replaced and 28 of 72 posts were vacant; OMB declined FY2026 funding for the IG council (CIGIE) in Oct 2025, then partly reversed (excerpts).

sub_claims.statement: GAO or the courts have made findings about these officials' ethics compliance.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: none found. The only court finding in scope concerns the IG removals (above). GAO's findings in 2025-2026 concern the Impoundment Control Act (for example a second violation found in June 2025; Federal News Network, excerpt), not any official's holdings. On 16 Nov 2026 the President nominated Eric Ueland, OMB deputy director and former acting OGE head, to lead GAO for 15 years; a hearing was set for 19 Nov and Democrats called the selection process a 'sham' (NOTUS, read in full).

sub_claims.statement: Any authority has found that one of these officials violated 18 U.S.C. 208 or an ethics agreement.
sub_claims.finding: No OGE, inspector-general, court, DOJ or congressional-committee finding of a violation by Musk, Patel, Kennedy, Oz, Hegseth, Wright, Burgum, McMahon, Loeffler, Bisignano, Isaacman or Boulos was found as of 17 Nov 2026. The documented items are waivers, agreements, letters, complaints and self-certified late reports. Holding an asset, or reporting a trade late, is not by itself a conflict-of-interest violation. With OGE led by acting heads or vacant for most of the term, the absence of findings is not exoneration.

corrections: C103 records CREW's 18 May 2026 letter as addressed to 'OGE Acting Director Eric Ueland'. CREW did address it that way, but senators wrote on the same day that Ueland's acting service had ended in early December 2025 and that OGE had no acting head; Keith Sonderling was named acting director on 23 June 2026. Suggested wording: 'addressed to Eric Ueland as acting director (senators said his acting service had ended in Dec 2025)'.

C65 (Patel) can add from his ethics agreement (read in full): he keeps Elite Depot (Shein parent) stock units under an agency 'remote' determination, agreed to resign from the Trump Media board, and has a one-year covered relationship with Qatar after embassy consulting that ended in Nov 2024. No change to C65's verdict.
C68 (Musk) can add that no 208(b)(1) waiver for Musk appears on the White House waiver list and that his disclosure was confidential; no correction to its figures.
C86: no overlap found; no correction.
Claimed: Bisignano divested late. The record shows: his Fiserv sales (16 May to 1 July 2025) were inside the 120-day window; the dispute is about timing before the stock's fall, not lateness.
Claimed: Isaacman divested his Shift4 stake. The record shows: his ethics agreement lets him keep it with reduced voting control and recusal.
denials_and_context: HHS says it confirmed Kennedy's compliance in May 2025; Kennedy says he gave up the fee interest before taking office.
The SBA says Loeffler's portfolio is independently managed without her direction and that she meets all ethical and legal requirements.
Bisignano's agency says he complied with all obligations of his ethics agreement.
The Pentagon denies that Hegseth or his representatives approached BlackRock; the FT stands by its report.
The White House said in Feb 2025 that Musk would excuse himself from conflicting contracts and was filing the required disclosure.

Late 278-T counts come from the officials' own certifications as tallied by Open Cabinet, a third-party tracker; a late report is a reporting lapse with a $200 fee, not a late divestiture or a conflict violation.
The PSI figure is a minority staff estimate, and the IG vacancy counts come from advocacy groups and think tanks with differing denominators.
An absence of findings is not exoneration: OGE was led by acting heads or vacant for most of the term, and many IG posts were vacant.
